SCORE CONVENTION. GUT is reported on the stated 0-10 scale (0.6 x ferment ladder 0-4, plus 0.4 x plant-type count capped at 19, which tops out at exactly 10). For INF the two stated ladders (0-3 and 0-7) do not sum to 10 on raw values, so I normalised each sub-ladder to 0-10 before weighting: INF = 0.6 x (omega3/3 x 10) + 0.4 x (diversity/7 x 10). If the existing sixty used raw ladder values instead, divide my INF figures by roughly 2.17 before merging.

THE HEADLINE FINDING. The vinegar-sauce hypothesis holds. Every eastern-style plate here lands at 6.5-7 g of sugar, where the same meat under a Kansas City sauce would add 12-16 g. But vinegar buys nothing on sodium, and sodium is what actually breaks NC barbecue: all four barbecue and soul-food plates sit between 1,740 and 2,120 mg, mostly from pit seasoning and from pork-cooked vegetables. A chopped-pork plate ordered with the vinegar and with greens instead of hush puppies and mac is a defensible order on sugar, calories and protein density, and an indefensible one on salt. No ordering choice available to a customer fixes that.

THE FATBACK QUESTION, ANSWERED. Southern greens are not a free vegetable. At Backyard BBQ Pit the collards and green beans together contribute roughly 4.4 of the plate's 7.0 g of saturated fat and about 1,000 of its 1,900 mg of sodium — more saturated fat than the smoked turkey itself. They still earn their place on fiber and plant count, but they are a seasoned dish, not a side salad.

THE VEGETABLE PLATE IS NOT THE GOOD ORDER. Backyard BBQ Pit sells a "Veggie Plate (4 sides)" at $16.24 on DoorDash. I excluded it deliberately: four pork-seasoned sides deliver roughly 10-14 g of protein against 1,800+ mg of sodium, failing the 30 g protein bar while gaining nothing on salt. At a Southern counter the lean smoked bird beats the vegetable plate on every criterion including the plant criteria, because the bird plate still comes with two vegetables.

CATEGORIES I FOUND NOTHING USABLE IN.

Lexington-style shoulder with red dip: no delivering representative in the Triangle. Lexington-style is Piedmont food; the Triangle is eastern-style territory and its houses are whole-hog or shoulder-with-vinegar. Allen & Son in Chapel Hill is the nearest thing and its sauce is explicitly tomato-free, so it is not a Lexington representative either. This is a genuine regional gap, not a research failure — do not pad it.

Catfish: I found fried catfish widely (The Pit, Sam Jones as a sandwich, most soul-food counters) and no baked, grilled or blackened catfish plate on any Triangle delivery menu I could verify. Fried catfish would score in the low ranges on LIV and ENE and would add nothing the fried wings do not already demonstrate, so I left the slot empty rather than fill it.

Fried-chicken places that also sell grilled or roasted birds: the Triangle's fried-chicken specialists (Bojangles, Beasley's, the soul-food counters) fry exclusively. Nobody in the category runs a rotisserie or grill alongside. The roasted-bird slot in this region is filled by the barbecue smokehouses instead, which is why two of my five entries are smoked poultry rather than one — Sam Jones's sliced breast and Backyard's vinegar-chopped turkey are genuinely different dishes with different sauce regimes and different sodium profiles, not a duplicate.

Grilled wings: do not exist in the Triangle as far as I could establish. Smoked wings do exist at Lawrence Barbecue and at Sam Jones, but Lawrence's menu states outright that theirs are "Smoked & Fried", and a food-writer account confirms the sauce goes on after the fryer. I did not verify Sam Jones's wing preparation and so did not score it. Treat "smoked wings" on a Triangle menu as a flavor claim, not a cooking-method claim, unless the kitchen says otherwise.

PRICE BASIS WARNINGS. The Pit ($17.50) and Lawrence ($17.00) are restaurant-menu prices and will run roughly 15-25% higher on a delivery app. Sam Jones ($20.90) and Let's Eat ($18.11) are delivery-platform prices already. Backyard's $16.79 is the only figure I could not tie to the specific dish — it is their DoorDash BBQ Pork Plate price used as a category proxy, and the turkey plate may differ.

Categories I could not fill honestly. GEORGIAN: nothing operating inside the named area. The Triangle's khachapuri points to Karavan by 3 Olives, which is in Garner, outside Raleigh/Durham/Cary/Morrisville/Chapel Hill/Apex/RTP, and Silk Road Uzbek is already entry 60. No Georgian restaurant found in-area. ARMENIAN: none found — a Cary listing that aggregators tag "Israeli, Armenian, Georgian, Tatar and other specialty foods of Central Asia" resolves to a grocery/deli rather than a restaurant with an orderable prepared menu, so I did not use it. ISRAELI: no dedicated Israeli restaurant found in the area; the sabich/shakshuka/hummusiya category is genuinely absent and the Levantine entries the compendium already has (Sassool, Baba Ghannouj, Neomonde) are the nearest thing. YEMENI: included, but it is the shakiest of the five — the business at 3933 Western Blvd appears to have relaunched from "Yemen Arab Restaurant" (older Yelp entry now flagged CLOSED) to "Yemen Arabic Restaurant" (Yelp updated May 2026, Sept 2025 press, live on three delivery apps). Worth a phone call before printing.

Two accuracy caveats on what I did return. (1) PRICES: Flame Kabob, Kipos and Talullas prices are read off the restaurants' own current menus, which are counter prices — DoorDash will run above them. The Halal Guys Cary price is an estimate and flagged as such: the chain does not publish prices, franchisees set their own, and no Cary-specific figure could be verified beyond a February 2026 review reporting ~$18 for a regular platter plus a soda. Yemen Arabic's is from the Uber Eats listing, i.e. already a delivery price. (2) DOORDASH: every store ID returned was found in an indexed DoorDash store URL; DoorDash itself serves a Cloudflare challenge to any direct fetch, so I could not open the live pages to confirm current menu, pricing or open/closed state. Kipos returned no DoorDash page at all on targeted search — they run direct ordering on Toast and their Uber Eats page (under their old W Franklin address) shows unavailable, so I marked it likely_but_unconfirmed rather than claiming either way. Talullas has an indexed DoorDash page but appears possibly inactive there, and their own NetWaiter ordering page returns "Online Ordering Not Available".

One deliberate scoring note: the Kipos entry is chicken souvlaki, not their SOLOMOS (wood-fired salmon with spanakorizo, $30) or BRANZINO ($45), both of which would score higher on health. Souvlaki is what the brief asked for and it is the honest Greek archetype — but if you want the best-scoring dish on that menu rather than the most representative one, it is the Solomos, and the swap is worth making explicit in the text.

The Halal Guys is the only one of the five that publishes nutrition, and I used the official January 2023 guide PDF directly. Its numbers are the platter rows only; the sauces are separate rows, which is how the 600 kcal / 56 g fat cost of the two included white sauce packets on a regular platter can be stated exactly rather than estimated.

WHAT I FOUND NOTHING USABLE IN, and why.

SOMALI, ERITREAN AND SUDANESE — genuinely empty. Searching Somali, Eritrean and Sudanese restaurants across Raleigh, Durham, Cary and Chapel Hill returns only Ethiopian houses (Goorsha, Nafkot, Abol) plus Awazé Cuisine in Cary, which markets itself as "Ethiopian and Eritrean" but is an injera-and-wot kitchen indistinguishable in construction from the two Ethiopian entries the compendium already scores. There is no standalone Somali or Sudanese restaurant in the Triangle that I could establish. The nearest Somali restaurant that surfaced at all was Jamile's in Charlotte, which is out of area. This category should be reported as absent, not padded.

GHANAIAN — also empty as a standalone cuisine. No Ghanaian restaurant in the Triangle could be established. Waakye, kelewele and Ghanaian light soup appear on no menu I could verify. What the Triangle actually has under "West African" is Nigerian (Chop Naija Kitchen, Gifted Hands Cuisine, Tasty Nigerian Cuisine, Nigeria Kitchen LLC in Wake Forest, Elle Et Moi) and Senegalese (Hady's, Yagg Sii Tenn in Apex). The compendium should say West African means Nigerian and Senegalese here.

TWO WEST AFRICAN PLACES I CHECKED AND DROPPED FOR EVIDENCE REASONS, not because they are bad:
- Yagg Sii Tenn, 1440 Chapel Ridge Rd Ste 170, Apex. Real and open — Yelp updated April 2026 with 148 photos and 67 reviews, Tripadvisor listing, its own Squarespace site last modified 2026-07-20, and an active DoorDash store (25629950). Senegalese executive chef, pan-African menu, reviewers name vegan yassa and chicken karanga. I could not retrieve a single priced menu item: the site has no menu page, and Seamless, Zmenu, Grubhub, Restaurant Guru and DoorDash all blocked retrieval. Rule 3 says do not invent a menu item, so it is out. It is the most promising unscored West African address in the region and worth a phone call.
- Gifted Hands Cuisine, 3600 N Duke St Ste 35, Durham. Real and open (own site, Discover Durham directory, Yelp updated June 2026, DoorDash store 31910051, Uber Eats). Nigerian plus Jamaican. Their own site lists categories only — "Soup: Egusi or Ogbono soup with goat, fish or turkey meat" and "Seafood: fish and shrimps fried, grilled, or skewered" — and every route to per-item prices was blocked; the only figures I could reach were catering trays ($140 for a half pan of efo riro), which is not a fast-casual order. Also out on rule 3.

TASTY NIGERIAN CUISINE, Raleigh — excluded deliberately. Real, but its own delivery terms are Zone 1 $15 fee with a $150 minimum rising to $35 and a $250 minimum. That is a catering operation, not delivery food, and it does not belong in this compendium.

CARIBBEAN — one lead I could not confirm and want flagged rather than used. Golden Krust at 4412 Fayetteville Rd, Raleigh is real, open (Mon-Sat 11-8, Sun 11-7) and on DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub and Postmates. A secondary source describes a "Steam Snapper Fish — perfectly steamed red snapper with spices, onions, carrots and peppers" at that location, but Golden Krust's own national menu at goldenkrust.com lists only Escovitch Fish and no steamed snapper, and callaloo appears only as "Callaloo & Saltfish" on the breakfast menu. Franchise menus vary; I could not verify steam snapper on the Raleigh store's own menu, so I did not score it. If someone confirms it by phone it is probably a better entry than Mum's, since Golden Krust's steamed-vegetables side is a real menu item.

CALLALOO AS A SIDE — asked and answered: no. At Mum's it is sold only cooked down with codfish as a dish. At Golden Krust it is a breakfast item with saltfish. I found no Triangle Caribbean kitchen selling plain callaloo as an orderable vegetable side. Jerk fish likewise does not exist here as a menu item; jerk is chicken and occasionally pork, and the fish preparations on offer are escovitch (fried), brown stew and steamed. That is why the steamed order is the whole play.

BRAZILIAN — the rodízio problem is real. Brasa, Estampa Gaucha, Leblon and Rio Brazilian Steakhouse are dine-in all-you-can-eat formats; none sells a grilled cut with the salad bar as a delivery item, and Grill Brazil at Triangle Town Blvd is marked closed on Yelp as of June 2026. Boteco do Brazil in Cary is the single place I found that will sell you grilled picanha alongside a salad rather than a buffet, and its $9 add-on line is what makes that entry possible at all.

ONE CORRECTION FOR THE EXISTING EDITION: if the compendium carries any Zweli's entry pointing at 4600 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd or 905 W Main St, both are closed. The operating restaurant is Zweli's Ekhaya at 406 Blackwell St in the American Tobacco Campus, and the two DoorDash pages still carrying the Zweli's name point at the dead addresses — one of them explicitly flagged inactive. I left the DoorDash field empty for that entry rather than reuse a stale id.

ON THE PRICES: all five are delivery-era prices and all five run above the counter. Hady's $27.29 is unambiguously a marked-up delivery figure (the .29 / .79 / .09 endings across their whole menu are markup arithmetic). Mum's $23.99 comes off a restaurant site whose footer still reads 2015, so the real counter price is likely higher, not lower. Chop Naija, Zweli's Ekhaya and Boteco prices came off menus the restaurants currently publish themselves.

METHOD NOTE, because it shaped what I could and could not return. The session's web-search budget was exhausted after two queries, and DoorDash, Yelp business pages, Tripadvisor, Uber Eats, MenuPix, Restaurantji, Zmenu, Sirved and the Wayback Machine all refuse automated fetches from this environment. Everything below was therefore established from three sources that do respond: restaurants' own websites, the Grubhub-owned Allmenus menu mirror, and — the most valuable find — Wake County Environmental Health's public restaurant-inspection ArcGIS service at maps.wakegov.com, which gives permit status, address, facility type and dated inspection scores for every operating food business in Wake County. That is why the Wake County entries carry hard "still open as of a 2025-26 inspection" evidence and the two Durham entries rely on live websites instead.

TAIWANESE — real kitchens found, no quotable menu, so no entry. Three Taiwanese businesses are provably operating: TAIPEI CAFE, 9825-G Chapel Hill Rd, Morrisville (Wake HSISID 04092016932, inspected 2026-05-15, score 90.5; its own site taipeicafenc.com was served to me today, 2026-08-28, per its cache header); TAIPEI AUTHENTIC CHINESE CUISINE, 121 E Chatham St, Cary (HSISID 04092016148, inspected 2026-05-18, score 97.5 — this is the address Allmenus still files under the old name "Taipei 101"); and LOVE BAO TAIWANESE KITCHEN, 1961 High House Rd, Cary, permitted as a food stand. I could not quote a dish from any of them. Taipei Cafe serves its menu only through a MealKeyway JavaScript ordering app with no server-rendered fallback; the Cary restaurant's domain taipei101nc.com returned Cloudflare 522 (origin unreachable) on every attempt all session; Love Bao has no reachable web menu; and Q Noodles in Cary (1026 Ryan Rd, live site with posted hours) hides its menu behind the same class of SPA. Rule 3 forbids me naming a dish I have not seen on a menu, and a Tripadvisor reviewer saying "get the beef noodle soup" is not a menu. Worth saying for the next pass: a Taiwanese beef noodle soup would almost certainly have scored badly anyway — braised beef shank in a soy-and-spice broth is a 2,000-2,500 mg sodium bowl before you touch the pickled mustard greens, and lu rou fan is fatty pork belly over white rice. The vegetable sides (sauteed A-cai, water spinach with garlic) are the good order there, and they are not meals.

MALAYSIAN, INDONESIAN, SINGAPOREAN — genuinely absent, not padded. I found no dedicated Malaysian, Indonesian or Singaporean restaurant in Raleigh, Durham, Cary, Morrisville, Chapel Hill, Apex or RTP whose existence I could establish. The only Malaysian cooking I could evidence anywhere in the seven towns is the crossover section at Road To Myanmar — its menu lists Char Kau Teo ($16.50+), Bak Kut Teh ($19.99), Wonton Mee Kondo ($18.00), Wonton Mee Soup ($18.00) and Pal Prata w/ chickpeas — and that restaurant is already used above for its Burmese entry. No gado-gado, no nasi campur, no laksa, and no satay sold as anything but a three-skewer appetiser. Treat this as a real hole in the region rather than a hole in the search. Gado-gado in particular would have scored extremely well (peanut sauce, tempeh, blanched vegetables, a live ferment) and there is nowhere to order it.

CHINESE-AMERICAN DIET MENUS — the survey behind the Golden Dragon pick. I pulled and grepped seventeen Raleigh Chinese takeout menus. Only four print a Diet section at all: Golden Dragon, China Pearl (2841 Jones Franklin Rd), Fu Kee Express (6320 Capital Blvd) and Jumbo China (8521 Cantilever Way). China Pearl's is the cheapest version of the identical D1-D6 block — D6 at $12.09 — but its website bestchinapearl.com no longer resolves and I could not confirm current operation, so I did not use it. Peking Garden on W Millbrook has no Diet section but does something more interesting: a build-your-own steamed fish (grouper, salmon, yellowfin, mahi) with a choice of sauces and steamed broccoli, which is a better dish and a worse fit for the "standard takeout place" question the reader actually asked. The answer to that question is yes, there is one good order, and it is the same order at every one of these places.

CANTONESE — partial yes. Dim Sum House is the only kitchen I found running a real congee list (five of them, off the dim sum sheet). But there is no whole steamed fish with ginger and scallion anywhere I looked; Dim Sum House's own seafood section is Sichuan-leaning — Boiled Fish with Napa in Chili Oil and Sliced Fish Fillet and Silken Tofu in Szechuan Hot Oil, both $19.00. So: proper Cantonese dim sum and congee, yes; proper Cantonese steamed fish, no. Note also that the congee entry above is the one place I broke the one-dish rule — a $7.25 bowl of rice porridge is not a meal, and I built it up to one with gai lan and har gow rather than pretend otherwise. Score it as the three-item order it is.

FILIPINO — why Krill and not the obvious choice. FILIPINO EXPRESS RESTAURANT, 3601 Capital Blvd Ste 101, Raleigh, is real and thriving (Wake HSISID 04092016646, inspected 2026-08-25 at 96.0, and twice more in the past year), and it is the Filipino grocery-and-counter the region actually eats at. Its menu is short and almost entirely fried or fatty: Chicken BBQ $3.25, BBQ Pork $3.25, Grilled Pork Belly $11, Lechon Kawali 1lb $10, Adobo Pork $9, Fried Tilapia $9, Sweet and Sour Tilapia $12, Pancit $7. No sinigang, no pinakbet, no inihaw na isda. The Chicken BBQ is the honest lean order there and it is a $3.25 skewer, not a meal. Krill is the only place in the Triangle I could evidence with sinigang on a standing menu, which is why the Filipino entry costs $28 instead of $10 — a real cost signal the compendium should probably say out loud.

PRICE CAVEAT. Three of the five prices (Golden Dragon, Dim Sum House, Twisted Noodle) come from the Allmenus/Grubhub mirror of those restaurants' menus rather than from a live checkout, because none of those three sells through a scrapeable ordering page. I marked them restaurant_menu_seen because they are the restaurant's own printed prices, but the mirror can lag by a year or more. Twisted Noodle's block reads current (Pad Thai at $18.00); Golden Dragon's and Dim Sum House's read like 2023-24 and are probably one increase behind. Road To Myanmar's $14.99 and Krill's $28 came off the restaurants' own live sites today. None of these five restaurants publishes nutrition data; all six macros in every entry are my estimates from dish construction.

RESEARCH CONSTRAINTS, stated up front because they bound every confidence rating. This session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before I made a single call, so all discovery ran through WebFetch. Google, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Ecosia, Mojeek and Yelp all returned 403/CAPTCHA; Bing returned Chicago-geolocated results for every Triangle query and was useless. What worked was (a) the OpenStreetMap Overpass and Nominatim APIs, which I used to enumerate every restaurant in a Triangle bounding box tagged peruvian, colombian, cuban, salvadoran, honduran, dominican, puerto_rican, venezuelan or latin_american, plus name-matches on marisco/cevich/cubano/parrilla/pupus/arepa, and (b) Yahoo search, which resolved locally and correctly. DoorDash itself was 403 on every attempt, so I captured NO store ids and have invented none; every doordash_status is what I could actually establish from third-party evidence, and four of five are "likely_but_unconfirmed".

CATEGORIES I FOUND NOTHING USABLE IN.

Argentine or Uruguayan grill: there is none. Overpass returns zero restaurants tagged argentinian, uruguayan or brazilian anywhere in the seven-town area, and a Yahoo sweep for churrascaria/parrilla/Uruguayan in Raleigh, Cary, Durham, Morrisville, Chapel Hill and Apex surfaced only national chains (Fogo de Chão, Terra Gaucha, Chima, Bullvino's) with no Triangle location. The entire Argentine presence is two baked-empanada shops — Makus Empanadas (Durham + Raleigh) and Che Empanadas (Transfer Co Food Hall and Duraleigh Corners, Raleigh) — and neither is a grill. I returned Makus as the honest representative and it scores at the bottom of the book. Uruguayan: nothing at all, in any source.

Colombian: nothing worth returning. Overpass finds no restaurant tagged colombian in the bounding box, and Yahoo turned up no Triangle Colombian storefront with a fetchable menu. The nearest things are Venezuelan — Guasaca (already at rank 16), Pabellon Arepas and Bowls and D'Lujo Grill (both 2312 New Raleigh Hwy, Durham), and Empanadas and More (2107 Grace Park Dr, Morrisville) — so the arepa end of the region is already represented. Bandeja paisa, ajiaco and sancocho do not appear on any Triangle menu I could reach.

Puerto Rican and Dominican: real but unfetchable. OSM confirms Fall River Cafe (10630 Durant Rd, Raleigh, tagged puerto_rican) and The Dominicans Restaurant (3601 Capital Blvd Unit 107, Raleigh, tagged dominican) as existing businesses, but I could not reach a menu for either, and mofongo — the dish the sweep asked about — is a fried-plantain mash that would score near the Makus floor anyway. I chose Cuban to carry this bullet because Carmen's publishes a full priced menu and sits in Morrisville, minutes from RTP.

Honduran: La Cacerola, 2014 Guess Road, Durham, is tagged honduran in OSM and is the only Honduran restaurant in the area. No fetchable menu, so I could not verify a dish and did not return it. I gave the second-Central-American slot to Pupuseria Doña Laura instead, which has three Durham storefronts and a published menu.

ON THE CURTIDO QUESTION, which was the sharpest thing you asked. Curtido is available elsewhere — Pupuseria Doña Laura advertises it heavily ("the most flavorful curtido"), and Samantha's Pupusas (Hillsborough, outside the seven towns) and El Curtido are the other Salvadoran options. But at Doña Laura it is welded to the pupusa order and appears nowhere on the menu as a standalone side, so you cannot have it alongside the grilled breast without buying 800 calories of masa. More importantly, I could not establish for ANY of them whether the curtido is a genuine lacto-ferment or a same-day vinegar slaw, and the compendium's own rule gives vinegar quick-pickles zero. I have therefore scored Doña Laura's ferment ladder at 0 rather than guess. El Cuscatleco's rank-2 position rests on a ferment credit of 3; if that credit was itself assumed rather than verified, it is worth a phone call, because it is carrying about 4.5 points of GUT on its own.

TWO MARISCOS CANDIDATES, one returned. Mariscos Los Cabos Bar and Grill (4020 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd, Durham) is the one I returned — richest and most specific menu, exact dish name and price, closest to RTP. The alternative is Mariscos El Patron 323 (421 Chapanoke Rd #103, Raleigh, plus a Smithfield site), which has stronger existence evidence — its own live site with current hours (Sun–Thu 11–8, Fri–Sat 11–9), phone (919) 803-8567, and a statement on that site that it delivers via GrubHub, DoorDash and Uber Eats — but a much terser menu ("CHAROLAS $18 — Shrimp, Octopus, Fish or Aguachile"; "TOSTADAS $11"). A Visit Raleigh listing also describes it operating as a food truck four days a week, which makes it a less reliable delivery proposition. If Los Cabos' aggregator price turns out stale, El Patron 323's $18 charola de aguachile is the drop-in substitute at essentially the same macros and a worse COST score. A third, Mariscos Nayarit (3351 Cypress Plantation Trail, Raleigh), is definitely operating — own site with hours, present in OSM, listed on Grubhub, Seamless, Uber Eats and on order.online (DoorDash's white-label storefront product) — but its entire menu is posted as images, so I could not read a single dish name or price and would not guess at one.

PERUVIAN, AND WHETHER THE SIDES SWAP. Yes, and cleanly. Alpaca's combos include two sides drawn from a $4.75 "regular" tier that contains black beans and house salad alongside fries and white rice, so the swap is free; green beans, yuca fries, tostones and maduros sit in a $5.25 premium tier and cost extra. That single fact is what moves a quarter chicken from a fries-and-rice plate to a 53-gram-protein meal at 515 calories. Two other Peruvian rotisserie options exist and I did not chase them: Mami's Latin Style Rotisserie Chicken (2401 Wake Forest Rd, Raleigh) and Lucky Chicken (1851 N Harrison Ave, Cary), both tagged peruvian in OSM. Also noted for a future sweep: IKA, a Peruvian-Japanese Nikkei kitchen in Raleigh, which would be a genuinely different proposition from either Mi Perú or Alpaca.

A CAVEAT ON THE SHAPE OF THIS BATCH. Two of the five entries are raw cured seafood, which only partly answers the reader's complaint. In defence: aguachile and ceviche are composed regional dishes with fixed constructions, not build-your-own bowls, and they are genuinely where the lean orders live in Mexican-seafood and Cuban kitchens. But if you want the batch to read as more varied, Alpaca and Doña Laura are the two that most change the book's texture, and both are hot plates off a fire.

TOOLING CAVEAT, because it shapes what follows. This session's web-search budget was exhausted before I began, and Google, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Mojeek, Ecosia, Yelp, TripAdvisor, DoorDash, Grubhub, Uber Eats and Toast all returned 403s or bot challenges to direct fetches. I worked instead from OpenStreetMap's Overpass API (structured, addressed, with opening hours and website tags) and then fetched restaurants' own sites, PDFs and JS bundles. That is why every existence claim below cites either a live first-party site or an OSM record with a street address, and why only one DoorDash store ID appears.

DOORDASH. Every doordash.com page returned 403. The single store ID I have (BLR Food Street, 33662053) came from a DoorDash link published on the restaurant's own site. For the other five I have marked likely_but_unconfirmed rather than guess an ID. One caveat worth printing: The Fiction Kitchen's own site directs all takeout to Toast and names no delivery partner at all, so it may genuinely not be on DoorDash.

BANGLADESHI — NOTHING FOUND. An Overpass sweep of the whole Triangle bounding box for cuisine=bangladeshi returned zero results, and no name in the region matched Bengal, Dhaka, Bengali or Kolkata. I could not establish that a Bangladeshi restaurant operates in the area and I have not invented one. Grand Malabar stands in for the fish-curry and omega-3 gap the sweep identified, and it is a better answer than a token entry would have been: Kerala meen curry is a real regional fish preparation, not a fish garnish on a north Indian menu.

SRI LANKAN — NOTHING FOUND. cuisine=sri_lankan returned zero across the bounding box; no name matched Ceylon, Lanka or Kottu. If there is a Sri Lankan kitchen in the Triangle it is not mapped and not indexed anywhere I could reach. Treat this as a genuine gap, not a scored category.

PAKISTANI — EXISTS, BUT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT A DISH. Two Pakistani houses are real and open: Kababish Cafe, 201 W Chatham St Suite 103, Cary (OSM hours Mo/We/Th 16:00-21:00, Tu closed, Fr-Su 12:00-21:00; live site; halal-certified), and Kabab & Curry, 2412 Hillsborough St, Raleigh, with a second Durham location. Both put their menus behind Cloudflare or a JavaScript ordering widget, and every aggregator mirror was blocked. OSM also records an unnamed cuisine=pakistani retail unit at 748 Ninth Street, Durham. Rule 3 says do not invent a menu item, so there is no Pakistani entry — but the charcoal boti and seekh the sweep asked about are there to be scored on a session with working search. This is the single biggest hole left.

CHAAT — THE ANSWER IS: MOSTLY FRIED, AND IT CANNOT MAKE THE PROTEIN BAR. I read BLR Food Street's full Morrisville menu, all 90-odd items. The Chatpata Junction section is puri shells, sev, samosa, vada pav and pav bhaji; the highest-protein thing on the whole board is paneer, and the whole menu is vegetarian with no meat, egg or fish anywhere. The best complete-meal chaat I could construct clears 18 g of protein, well short of 30. Dahi puri and the tikki chaat do carry real live yogurt and that is worth its gut credit, but the category is a snack category and scores like one. That is the finding. I looked for a protein-forward alternative — Honest Indian Vegetarian (3607 Davis Drive, Morrisville, real and open, OSM diet:vegetarian=only) and Nukkad (1710 High House Road, Cary) both trade in the same format, and Honest's menu sits behind Toast, which was blocked.

VEGAN, BEYOND THE ONE I SCORED. The Triangle has more of this than the compendium admits: Pure Soul Vegan (4125 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd, Durham), Banu Vegan (2534 S Roxboro St, Durham), Vegan Community Kitchen (803 E Williams St, Apex), Pure Vegan Cafe (Raleigh/Durham, Creedmoor Rd), Dirty V (301 Glenwood Ave, Raleigh) and Element Gastropub (421 Fayetteville St, Raleigh) all carry diet:vegan=only in OSM. I scored the one with a fully published, priced menu. There is a second sweep's worth of material here.

BREAKFAST. Genuinely thin for delivery. The mapped field is IHOP, Biscuitville, Rise, Sutton's, Famous Toastery and First Watch, which the compendium already has. Another Broken Egg is the pick because it is the only one that publishes a complete nutrition table, and the numbers are far better than the category's reputation — but note the same table shows their Southern Breakfast Bowl at 1,370 kcal and 4,500 mg of sodium, and the Benedict Burger at 5,830 mg. The category average is catastrophic; one dish on it is not.

PIZZA AND BURGERS SCORE ROUGHLY AS EXPECTED, WITH ONE SURPRISE. The margherita's flavour score, 8.2, is the highest number I produced in this sweep, and its protein is respectable — the reader was right to suspect the compendium was ducking it. Its calorie load is the problem, not its construction. Oakwood Pizza Box (610 N Person St, Raleigh) was the other serious pizza candidate but sells only 18-inch pies at $21, which is not a single meal. Pizzeria Faulisi in Cary has become a daytime caffè with 9am-3pm hours and was dropped for that reason.

PRICES I DID NOT SEE. Two of six are approximate and flagged: Grand Malabar publishes no priced menu anywhere on its site (only the $28.99 Onam Sadya), and Another Broken Egg's prices live behind a JavaScript Olo widget. Both are marked approximate_from_category and neither should be printed as a hard figure. Pizzeria Toro's $24 is a real menu price, but the menu also adds a 20 percent living wage fee to every check, so the true cost is nearer $28.80 before delivery markup — the cost score for that entry is therefore optimistic by about a point.
